notes:
Cliopatria rows: the Nicaean Empire row (1206-1278) starts two years late (1204) and runs seventeen years past the reconquest of Constantinople (25 July 1261), standing in for the restored Byzantine Empire because the byzantine-empire row has no shapes between 1226 and 1279. The 1260-1271 shape is cut at 1261 and the 1272-1278 shape marked wrong; the byzantine-empire dossier (a sibling) needs new keyframes for 1261-1278 built from these shapes plus Constantinople (flagged in the report). The 1206-1209 shape already includes David Komnenos' Paphlagonian coast (Nicaean only from 1212-14); the single 1210-1249 shape misses the Latin Mysian lobe (1211/14-1225), the 1225 recovery of Asia and the islands, Gallipoli and the Thracian coast (1235), Thessalonica and Macedonia (1246): new keyframes 1212, 1214, 1225, 1235 and 1246 are proposed. The 1250-1259 shape gives Nicaea the Albanian coast for the decade although Dyrrhachium was Nicaean only 1256 - February 1258, and omits Rhodes (a province from 1250).

Vassals recorded in the ledger (rule 4): Rhodes under the Gabalas (1233-1250), Thessalonica under John and Demetrios Komnenos Doukas (1242-1246). Suzerains: none. The Seljuk truce of 1211 and the Mongol-dominated Seljuk frontier after 1243 produced no border change on the pages opened.

Gaps and disagreements: Paphlagonia annexed 1212 (Nicaea and Antioch pages) or late 1214 (Nymphaeum page); the Treaty of Nymphaeum 1212 (Treadgold) or December 1214; Theodore I's death November 1221 (his page) or 1222 (main page); Poimanenon late 1223 or early 1224; Adrianople Nicaean 1225-1227 rests on the Vatatzes page (the Epirus dossier has the Epirote gain in 1225); the towns of the 1246 campaign and Tzurulum's changes of hands (1237, 1240, 1247) are not on the pages opened (confidence 1); Rhodes' suzerainty 'is only surmised'. Pages that would not load: 'Epirote-Nicaean conflict (1257-59)', 'Byzantine-Latin wars'. The 1259-1260 occupation of Epirus mirrors the Epirus dossier's events.

Gazetteer names used as coordinates or polygons because the gazetteer lacks them: Pegai, Cyzicus, Philadelphia (Alasehir), Antioch on the Meander, Heraclea Pontica/Amastris (Paphlagonian coast polygon), Gallipoli, Tzurulum, Lesbos, Chios, Samos, Kos, Vodena, Kastoria, Deabolis, Servia, Tzepaina, Veles, Mystras, Monemvasia, the Mani; Kalamos; the 1246 Macedonian conquests are a polygon.

Repairs of 2026-10-19 after the eu-05-d review (Paphlagonia timeline, agreed with empire-of-trebizond): the single 1210 correction (which described 1214-1224 but was in force from 1210) is split into _1210 (1210-1211, Paphlagonia out), new _1212 (1212-1213, Heraclea and Amastris in, 32.6E to the Sinope district still Trapezuntine, Latin lobe out) and new _1214 (1214-1224, Paphlagonia to 34.4E); the 1214 gain, the contest_end, the 1225 and 1235 polygons and the war zone now end at 34.4E (west edge of the Sinope district, Seljuk from 1 November 1214); the 1246, 1250 and 1260 corrections gained the same polygon because Cliopatria's 1250 and 1260 shapes stop at 33.19E and would have dropped the strip Nicaea took in 1214. The contest with Trebizond starts in 1208 (siege of Heraclea Pontica) in both dossiers; the Theodore I Laskaris page has a 1206 decision cut short by the Latins, no ground taken. A Pelagonia contest pair with principality-of-achaea (1259, no month: the Pelagonia infobox says 'Early summer or autumn of 1259'; the achaea dossier has June) was added to mirror principality-of-achaea /ledger/15-16; I disagree on substance (the ground was Nicaean and Epirote, no Achaean land was contested, the Epirus contest covers it) and the pair should go from both dossiers together if the achaea fixer drops its own.
